provenance.what_this_is: The rep-level fact that a run's usage rows can outnumber its delivered assistant messages because openclaw ran a SECOND session inside the same rep, and that session's transcript ships beside the delivered one at <run>/task_output/sessions/.
provenance.koji: Both koji lanes shipped usage_attribution status=failed. run_1: 224 rows selected, 164 assistant messages, 25 internal, 1 post-agent, 34 unmatched -- and its sessions/ directory holds one sibling transcript, fdcddd7e-afb8-4136-b97c-659f159dbb5c.jsonl, with EXACTLY 34 assistant messages. run_2 is the same shape with 2 and 2 (0cbc05b6-4d6c-4602-a9b9-917be97d1635.jsonl). Both siblings are registered under agent:main:chat with origin {label: heartbeat, provider: cron-event}: the agent's own cron tool scheduled a main-session systemEvent, the gateway enqueued it, and the HEALTH loop answered it on a session of its own.
provenance.the_join: Session files carry per-message usage the same way chat.jsonl does -- input/output/cacheRead/cacheWrite real, cost zeroed. Joining the surplus rows to the sibling's assistant messages on those four numbers is exact and unambiguous: across both lanes there is not one tuple collision between a sibling message and a delivered message, no repeated tuple inside either side, and the rows left after absorption are tuple-equal to the delivered transcript's assistant messages IN ORDER (164/164 and 152/152). Timestamps cannot do this job -- the agent clock shim puts the session's message clock tens of days from the sidecar's UTC ts.
provenance.willie: The control. willie_prince run_1 shipped attributed with rows_unmatched 0 and ALSO has a sibling transcript (bf0ce5c5-fbf0-49d8-9ef3-19f9dbd41dc4.jsonl, origin {label: heartbeat, provider: heartbeat}, one assistant message). Its single turn was one request, the sidecar named it heartbeat, and it was already booked to internal_calls -- so there is no surplus and nothing for a sibling to absorb. It must stay exactly as delivered.
provenance.rows_note: Rows are the real sidecar rows with run_key, model, reasoning_tokens and duration_s dropped; the first two are re-injected by the test from run_key/model, the last two are not read by the attribution path. Every column it does read is verbatim.
provenance.sessions_note: Session transcripts are trimmed to what the reader consumes: one entry per line in file order, each keeping its type, and message entries keeping role plus the verbatim usage block. Prompt and response text is dropped -- these turns are not in the delivered transcript and this fixture is not a place to put them. sessions.json keeps every registry field except skillsSnapshot.
provenance.messages_note: The delivered chat.jsonl's user/assistant messages in order: "user", or "a:<input>,<output>,<cacheRead>,<cacheWrite>" carrying that assistant message's OWN usage block verbatim. Those four numbers are real in the delivered artifact -- every one of koji run_1's 164 assistant messages bills non-zero -- and only the cost sub-block beside them is zeroed, which is what makes the leftover rows checkable against the transcript they belong to. Prompt text is not carried; the transcript-side detectors have their own fixtures.

koji_run_1.agent_finished_ts_note: Not in the artifact -- usage.json pops __agent_finished_ts__ before writing. Pinned between the last turn row (14:49:15.805731Z) and the trailing heartbeat row (14:49:23.184754Z), which is the single row the delivered post_agent_calls booked, tuple (2, 451, 0, 34475).
